title: Week 10 Analysis
subtitle: Hume jumps from 5th to 1st, and the top three are now separated by one point.
intro_paragraphs: Four divisions changed order this week, and Cadegn's 11-point lead is gone. Hume gained 18, the biggest week in the pool since Cadegn's +30 in Week 8, and is in 1st at 63. Mike T gained 9 and is also at 63, second only on a tiebreaker. Cadegn lost 3 and is 3rd at 62. Last week the gap from 1st to 2nd was 11; now the gap from 1st to 3rd is 1.

The Buccaneers, Bears, Eagles, and Broncos had byes, and three of them moved anyway. The Bears and Broncos were both in first last week and dropped without playing, and the Buccaneers moved up a spot from the couch.

fun_facts.heading: Hume Goes from 5th to 1st
fun_facts.body: Hume was tied for 5th, 20 points out, a week ago. This week Hume gained 9 in the NFC North, 9 in the AFC West, and 3 in the AFC North, and gave back only 3 in the NFC South. Hume and Mike T are both at 63 with one perfect division each, so the second tiebreaker decides it: Hume has three top-2 bonuses to Mike T's two. It's Hume's first time in 1st since Week 7.

fun_facts.heading: The AFC West Is an 18-Point Swing
fun_facts.body: Kansas City won, Denver had a bye, and both are now 7-2, with the Chiefs first on a tiebreaker. Hume and Mike T picked Chiefs-Broncos and each gained 9 (both teams exact plus the top-2 bonus). Cadegn and Dustin picked Broncos-Chiefs and each lost all 9 they had there. If those two teams flip back, it's the same 9 points going the other way for all four of them. Tom (Broncos second) gained 3, and Dilger and Farmer (Broncos first) lost 3. The Chargers also got their first win, so there are no winless teams left.

fun_facts.heading: Everyone Finally Scores in the NFC North
fun_facts.body: Last week all seven bettors had 0 points here. This week Detroit and Minnesota won, Chicago had a bye, and all three are 7-2, ordered Lions, Vikings, Bears on tiebreakers. Green Bay lost and is last at 6-4. All seven picked the Lions to win it, so everyone gets at least 3. Mike T and Dustin also had the Bears third, for 6. Hume is the only one who picked the Vikings second, which comes with the top-2 bonus, for 9.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn Loses the Lead
fun_facts.body: Cadegn gained 3 in the NFC North and 3 in the AFC North, but the 9 lost in the AFC West made it -3 for the week. Cadegn had led for five of the last six weeks. Cadegn still has the most perfect divisions (2, the AFC East and AFC South) and the most division-winner picks currently right (5 of 8), but tiebreakers only matter when points are tied, and Cadegn is one behind.

fun_facts.heading: Mike T and Hume Picked Almost the Same Way
fun_facts.body: Mike T and Hume have identical picks in four divisions: the AFC East, AFC South, AFC West, and NFC West. That's why they both got 9 from the Chiefs this week. Mike T still has the most exact hits in the pool, 15 of 32, one more than Hume. Where they differ, it cancels out: Hume is 3 ahead in the NFC North and the AFC North, and Mike T is 3 ahead in the NFC South and the NFC East.

fun_facts.heading: Dilger and Tom: Tied on Everything
fun_facts.body: Dilger and Tom are both at 51 and match on every tiebreaker: one perfect division, one top-2 bonus, two bottom-2 bonuses, and 12 exact hits. That's the second week in a row two bettors are fully tied (Tom and Hume last week). Dilger got there with a net zero: +3 each in the NFC North and AFC North, -3 each in the NFC South and AFC West. Tom gained 6, with +3 in the NFC South, NFC North, and AFC West and -3 in the AFC North.

fun_facts.heading: The AFC North and NFC South Change at the Top
fun_facts.body: Cincinnati won and Pittsburgh lost, so the Bengals (7-2) are first and the Steelers (6-3) second. The four bettors with the Bengals first (Dilger, Hume, Cadegn, Farmer) gained 3, and the three with the Bengals second (Mike T, Dustin, Tom) lost 3. In the NFC South, the Saints lost and the idle Buccaneers passed them on a tiebreaker, both at 3-6. That cost Mike T, Dilger, and Hume the 3 they had for the Saints in second, and gave 3 to Dustin and Tom, who have Tampa Bay second. Carolina won and is a game clear in first at 4-5.

fun_facts.heading: Dustin and Farmer
fun_facts.body: Dustin lost 9 in the AFC West and 3 in the AFC North, got 9 back in the NFC North and NFC South, and is 6th at 48, 3 behind the tie for 4th. Farmer gained 3 and is at 30, 18 behind Dustin. Farmer is still the only bettor without a perfect division, but the Bengals taking first gives Farmer 4 of 8 division-winner picks currently right (Bengals, Jaguars, Bills, Lions), tied with Hume for second-most.

fun_facts.heading: Locks Back Up to 4
fun_facts.body: With the Lions back in first, 4 of the 8 picks everyone agreed on are holding: the Bills first, the Patriots second, and the Cardinals last in their divisions, plus the Lions first. All seven bettors picked the Steelers third and the Browns last in the AFC North, and both are wrong right now: the Browns (6-4) are third and the Ravens (4-6) are last.

closing_paragraph: Hume, Mike T, and Cadegn are within a point of each other, and the AFC West alone could reshuffle all three: the Chiefs and Broncos are tied at 7-2, with 9 points going one way or the other for four bettors. The NFC North has three teams at 7-2 and the NFC South has two at 3-6, so very little is settled. Same time next Tuesday.
